beyond 5 fathoms...

events.region: Davis, UT; Weber, UT
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Davis County in northern Utah...
South Central Weber County in northern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 545 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas due
to heavy rainfall from strong thunderstorms. River or stream flows,
especially along the Weber River, are expected to rise.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 248 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Public reported minor flooding is already
occurring in the advisory area. Between 0.75 and 1.25 inches of
rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Ogden, Layton, Farmington, Hill Air Force Base, Roy, Clearfield,
Kaysville, South Ogden, Washington Terrace, Riverdale, South
Weber, Uintah, Weber State University, Sunset, Fruit Heights and
East Layton.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: West Slopes Sacramento Mountains Below 7500 Feet; Sacramento Mountains Above 7500 Feet; East Slopes Sacramento Mountains Below 7500 Feet
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south central New Mexico, including the
following areas, East Slopes Sacramento Mountains Below 7500 Feet,
Sacramento Mountains Above 7500 Feet and West Slopes Sacramento
Mountains Below 7500 Feet.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 48-hour rainfall observations shows a wide swath of 0.75-1.50"
across the US-70 corridor over the Sacramento Mountains. High
soil moisture will allow runoff to occur quickly with any
additional rounds of rain. Additional scattered showers and
thunderstorms are expected to develop over portions of Otero
County this evening and overnight, leading to localized flash
flooding. Areas that have already received excessive rainfall and
flooding recently such as Whitetail, Apache Summit, and Tularosa
Creek will be at highest risk.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
